name: Text to DNA Converter
short: Convert any text into a biological DNA sequence (A, C, G, T) and decode it back.
description: Free online text to DNA converter. Encode text as nucleotides using 2-bit binary mapping and decode it again. 100% in-browser processing.

howTo.title: Enter your text
howTo.text: Type or paste standard text into the Input Text field, or click 'Try an example' to load sample data.

howTo.title: Encode or Decode
howTo.text: Click 'Convert to DNA' to encode text into nucleotides (A, C, G, T), or paste a nucleotide sequence and click 'Convert to Text'.

howTo.title: Copy or Download
howTo.text: Inspect the generated sequence and nucleotide statistics, then click 'Copy' to copy the sequence to your clipboard.

faq.q: How does text get converted into DNA nucleotides?
faq.a: Text is encoded into UTF-8 bytes, each represented as 8 binary bits. Every 2 bits are mapped onto one of the four DNA nucleotide bases: 00 = Adenine (A), 01 = Cytosine (C), 10 = Guanine (G), and 11 = Thymine (T). Thus, 1 character produces 4 nucleotides.

faq.q: Can I convert DNA sequences back into readable text?
faq.a: Yes! The decoder reads the sequence in 4-nucleotide chunks (8 bits = 1 byte) and reconstitutes the original UTF-8 characters.

faq.q: Is synthetic DNA actually used for digital data storage?
faq.a: Yes, modern researchers at Harvard, MIT, and Microsoft store petabytes of archival data in synthesized DNA molecules due to DNA's incredible density and thousand-year longevity.

faq.q: Does my text leave my browser?
faq.a: Never. All conversions happen entirely on your computer using client-side JavaScript. No text is ever uploaded or logged.

python.intro: Encode strings to DNA and back using standard library bitwise operations and a 2-bit nucleotide lookup table.
python.tip: Formatting bytes with f'{b:08b}' gives clean 8-bit strings that slice naturally into 2-bit nucleotide pairs.

short: Encode and decode plain text, URLs, and binary files to Base64 safely in your browser.
description: Fast online Base64 encoder and decoder. Convert text and files to Base64 format and reverse Base64 strings to UTF-8. Client-side and secure.

howTo.text: Select 'Text Mode' to encode or decode text strings, or 'File Mode' to convert local files directly into Base64 data URLs.

faq.q: What is Base64 encoding?
faq.a: Base64 is a binary-to-text encoding scheme that translates binary data into an ASCII string using 64 printable characters (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, +, and /). It is widely used in MIME email attachments, Data URLs, and web APIs.

faq.q: Does Base64 provide encryption or security?
faq.a: No, Base64 is strictly an encoding format for data transmission, not encryption. Anyone can decode a Base64 string instantly.

faq.q: How does Base64 affect file size?
faq.a: Base64 represents 3 bytes of binary data using 4 ASCII characters, resulting in an approximate 33% increase in data size.

faq.q: Can I convert images to Base64 for inline HTML/CSS?
faq.a: Yes! Drag and drop any image (PNG, JPG, SVG, WebP) and check the 'Generate Data URL' checkbox to get ready-to-paste `data:image/...;base64,...` code.

python.intro: Use Python's built-in `base64` module to handle UTF-8 text and binary data conversions cleanly.
python.tip: Always encode text strings to bytes (e.g. .encode('utf-8')) before passing them to b64encode.

faq.q: What is the difference between binary text conversion and numeric conversion?
faq.a: Numeric conversion translates a single integer value (e.g. 255 = 11111111 = 0xFF). Text conversion translates each character into its 8-bit ASCII/UTF-8 byte value in sequence.

faq.q: Can it handle 64-bit and arbitrarily large numbers?
faq.a: Yes, our converter uses JavaScript BigInt to accurately process integers of arbitrary precision without floating point truncation.

faq.q: How does Hex byte grouping work?
faq.a: You can toggle space separation between bytes (e.g. `4F 6C 64`) for cleaner reading when inspecting network packets or memory dumps.

python.intro: Use Python's built-in `bin()`, `hex()`, `oct()`, and `int()` functions with explicit radix bases.
python.tip: Pass the base as the second argument to int(string, base), e.g. int('1010', 2) -> 10.

faq.q: What is the difference between encodeURI and encodeURIComponent?
faq.a: `encodeURI` preserves protocol characters like `https://`, `:`, and `/`, whereas `encodeURIComponent` escapes all special characters so the string can be safely passed inside a query parameter.

faq.q: What is Unix Epoch time?
faq.a: Unix time is the number of seconds that have elapsed since midnight UTC on January 1, 1970, not counting leap seconds.

faq.q: Does this tool support millisecond timestamps?
faq.a: Yes! The tool automatically detects whether your input has 10 digits (seconds) or 13 digits (milliseconds) and converts accordingly.

python.intro: Work with URL parameters and timestamps using Python's standard `urllib.parse` and `datetime` modules.
python.tip: Use datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(ts, tz=datetime.timezone.utc) to always work with timezone-aware datetimes.

faq.q: Which cryptographic hash is recommended for modern security?
faq.a: SHA-256 and SHA-512 from the SHA-2 family are the gold standards for checksums and digital signatures. Older algorithms like MD5 and SHA-1 should not be used for security-critical applications due to known collision vulnerabilities.

faq.q: How does this generator compute hashes in the browser?
faq.a: It uses the native browser Web Crypto API (`window.crypto.subtle.digest`), executing hardware-accelerated C++ crypto primitives directly on your device.

faq.q: Can I hash passwords with SHA-256?
faq.a: While SHA-256 is cryptographically one-way, password storage should utilize slow, salted key derivation algorithms like Argon2, bcrypt, or PBKDF2 to resist brute force.

python.intro: Generate industry-standard cryptographic hashes using Python's standard `hashlib` and `hmac` libraries.
python.tip: Always pass bytes to hashlib.sha256(data.encode('utf-8')) and call .hexdigest() for the human-readable string.

faq.q: What is the difference between Metric (SI) and Imperial systems?
faq.a: The Metric system uses base-10 multiples (meters, grams, liters), whereas the Imperial system uses traditional non-decimal divisions (inches, feet, pounds, ounces).

faq.q: What is the difference between MB and MiB in digital storage?
faq.a: Megabytes (MB) use decimal multiples (1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes = 10^6), while Mebibytes (MiB) use binary multiples (1 MiB = 1,048,576 bytes = 2^20).

faq.q: How accurate are the conversions?
faq.a: Conversions use exact NIST and BIPM conversion constants with IEEE 754 double precision floating point arithmetic.

python.intro: Build a universal unit converter by normalizing all measurements to standard base SI units.
python.tip: Converting through a base unit (e.g. Value -> Meters -> Target) requires only 2N conversion factors instead of N^2 pairings.

faq.q: What is the difference between RGB and CMYK?
faq.a: RGB is an additive color model used for digital screens (Red, Green, Blue light). CMYK is a subtractive color model used in color printing (Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, Key/Black ink).

faq.q: Why is HSL preferred by UI designers?
faq.a: HSL (Hue, Saturation, Lightness) aligns with human visual perception. Changing the lightness or saturation of a hue produces natural UI shades without altering the base color.

faq.q: What is a good WCAG contrast ratio for text?
faq.a: WCAG 2.1 Level AA requires a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text. Level AAA requires at least 7:1.

python.intro: Convert color strings between HEX and RGB using Python tuple unpacking and string formatting.
python.tip: Use tuple(int(hex_code[i:i+2], 16) for i in (0, 2, 4)) to cleanly parse a 6-digit hex string into RGB integers.

faq.q: What is kerf compensation in laser cutting?
faq.a: Kerf is the width of material vaporized by the laser beam (typically 0.1mm - 0.25mm). Without kerf compensation, finger joints fit loosely; VectorCutter adjusts joints so parts press-fit snugly.

faq.q: Is VectorCutter compatible with my laser software?
faq.a: Yes! VectorCutter produces clean, standard-compliant vector SVG files with organized cut/engrave stroke colors suitable for LightBurn, Glowforge, RDWorks, and Inkscape.
